Use `POST /v3/search`. The body targets the `identities` index and uses a `term` filter (for exact match) or a `query` string — both work for email lookups.

---

## Look up an identity by email

### Request

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/search
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "attributes.email:\"jane.doe@example.com\""
  }
}
```

The `query.query` field is an Elasticsearch query string. Quoting the value enforces an exact match — without quotes it would do a full-text search.

---

### Alternatively: use a `term` filter for a strict exact match

```json
{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "*"
  },
  "filters": {
    "attributes.email": {
      "type": "TERM",
      "terms": ["jane.doe@example.com"]
    }
  }
}
```

Use `filters` when you need guaranteed exact-match semantics (no tokenization) and want to combine multiple attribute conditions cleanly.

---

### Key body fields

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `indices` | Must be `["identities"]` to search the identity index |
| `query.query` | Elasticsearch query string; field names follow `attributes.<attrName>` for identity attributes |
| `filters` | Optional map of field → filter object for exact `TERM` or `RANGE` matches |
| `queryResultFilter` | Optional — use `includes`/`excludes` to limit which fields come back |
| `limit` / `offset` | Query-string params for pagination (max page 10 000; use `searchAfter` beyond that) |

---

### Common identity fields you can filter on

| Attribute | Query string field |
|---|---|
| Email | `attributes.email` |
| Display name | `displayName` |
| Employee number | `attributes.employeeNumber` |
| Manager | `managerRef.name` |
| Any custom attribute | `attributes.<yourAttrName>` |

---

### Required scope

`sp:search:read`

---

### Example: find by a custom attribute

```json
{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "attributes.department:\"Engineering\""
  },
  "queryResultFilter": {
    "includes": ["id", "name", "displayName", "attributes.email"]
  }
}
```

The response is an array of identity objects matching your query; each has an `id` you can use in subsequent API calls.

```answer-summary
endpoints:
  - method: POST
    path: /v3/search
    api_version: v3
auth_flow: OAuth2 bearer token
required_scopes: [sp:search:read]
key_parameters: [indices, query, filters, queryResultFilter, limit, offset]
```
